newsitem.title: USA: Figgie sells Snorkel unit to Omniquip.
newsitem.headline: Figgie sells Snorkel unit to Omniquip.

text.p: Figgie International Inc. has agreed to sell its Snorkel division to Omniquip International Inc. for $150 million plus the assumption of certain liabilities, the companies said Monday.
Snorkel is a leading producer of booms used, for example, to raise workers onto aircraft wings for maintenance or at construction sites, eliminating the need for scaffolding.
Snorkel, which Figgie acquired in 1971, has about 900 employees in St. Joseph, Mo.; Elwood, Kan.; Melbourne, Australia; and Levin, New Zealand, and reported sales of $158 million in 1996.
Port Washington, Wis.-based Omniquip, which went public on March 20, is the largest North American producer of boom equipment used for moving cargo and other materials.
The parties expect the sale to be completed within 45 days, subject to regulatory approval.

Figgie said it would use the sale proceeds to launch an aggressive growth strategy -- mainly acquisitions for its Scott Aviation unit, which makes respiratory systems and equipment for aviation, industrial, fire and government markets.
Figgie also said that in light of the decision to sell the Snorkel division, its board has decided to delay naming a new chief executive officer until the end of August.

"Figgie is a different company today," Chairman John Reilly said. "Before making our final decision, we want to re-evaluate each candidate to ensure that we choose a corporate leader whose skills match the future needs of this company."
He said the delay was simply a final review of the candidates and not the beginning of a new search process.
Scott Aviation President Glen Lindemann said the company has already identified and evaluated several acquisition targets, and plans to make a significant purchase in the third quarter.

"We are particularly looking at companies and product lines that serve respiratory and related markets. Acquisitions should increase our existing market share and offer significant growth opportunities -- both through international expansion and new product lines."
The division is seeking to leverage the Scott brand name, its distribution network, and core technologies, he added.
Figgie said the sale of Snorkel is not way related to the unsolicited acquisition proposal for Figgie made by Heico Holding, a Chicago-based privately owned company, on July 3.

Figgie also manufactures satellite-based guidance, navigation, instrumentation and communications systems for aviation, defence and commercial sectors through its Interstate Electronics division. In 1996, the Willoughby, Ohio-based company had revenues of $386 million.
Figgie's stock rose 12.5 cents to $14.25, while Omniquip edged down 12.5 cents to $23.375 on Nasdaq in the afternoon.
